q: 1. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a considerable depth from earth's surface are called
explain: Plutonic (intrusive) rocks cool very slowly deep underground, allowing large crystals to form, e.g. granite.

q: 2. The arrangement size and shape of the constituent mineral grains of a stone gives the information about its
explain: Texture refers specifically to the size, shape, and arrangement of mineral grains within a rock.

q: 3. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a relatively shallow depth from the earth's surface are called
explain: Hypabyssal rocks form when magma cools at shallow depths, between plutonic (deep) and volcanic (surface) rocks.

q: 4. The foliated structure is very common in
explain: Foliation (banded/layered texture) develops from directional pressure during metamorphism, seen in schist, gneiss, slate.

q: 5. A Natural material of construction obtained from rocks by any suitable method is called
explain: Stone is defined as a natural building material extracted and shaped from rock.

q: 6. Chemically, Marble is a type of
explain: Marble is metamorphosed limestone, composed chiefly of calcium carbonate, hence calcareous.

q: 7. Quartzite is a (metamorphic)
explain: Quartzite is metamorphosed sandstone, composed mainly of silica, making it siliceous.

q: 8. Basalt is
explain: Basalt forms from lava that cools rapidly at the earth's surface, making it extrusive igneous rock.

q: 9. The color of statuary marble used for sculptor's work is
explain: Statuary marble is valued for sculpture due to its pure white color and fine uniform texture.

q: 10. The rocks having alumina or clay as their major constituents are known as
explain: Argillaceous rocks are defined by clay/alumina as their dominant constituent, e.g. shale.

q: 11. Which of the following has the highest Moh's hardness number?
explain: Diamond has a Mohs hardness of 10, the maximum on the scale.

q: 12. The rock generally used for roofing, is
explain: Slate splits into thin, smooth, weather-resistant sheets, making it ideal for roofing.

q: 13. A good quality stone absorbs water less than
explain: A good building stone should absorb less than about 5% water by weight to ensure durability.

q: 14. A stone is rejected if it absorbs water more than
explain: A stone absorbing more than 15% water is considered too porous and unsuitable for construction.

q: 15. Stones used for ornamental work must be
explain: Soft stones are easier to carve and shape for detailed ornamental work.

q: 16. Stones used for the construction of retaining walls must be
explain: Heavy stones provide the mass needed to resist lateral earth pressure in retaining walls.

q: 17. In stone masonry, the stratified stones are so placed that the direction of pressure to the plane of bedding is
explain: Placing bedding planes perpendicular (at right angles) to the load direction gives maximum load-bearing strength.

q: 18. In arches, stratified stones are placed so that their planes are
explain: In arches, bedding planes are aligned radially so they lie perpendicular to the thrust line along the arch.

q: 19. The tendency of a stone is to split along
explain: Cleavage is the natural tendency of a stone to split along definite planes of weakness.

q: 20. According to NS, in 1 cu. m. brick masonry, number of bricks required is
explain: As per standard practice for modular bricks, about 560 bricks are needed per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 21. Pick up the constituent of good brick earth whose excess causes the raw bricks shrink and warp during drying and burning, from the following
explain: Excess lime forms lumps that absorb moisture and expand on burning, causing bricks to crack and warp.

q: 22. Porcelain is used as
explain: Porcelain's smooth, non-porous, vitrified surface makes it the standard material for sanitary fittings.

q: 23. The presence of sand in brick earth prevents
explain: Sand reduces the plasticity and shrinkage of clay, thereby preventing warping during drying and burning.

q: 24. The minimum compressive strength of 1st class bricks should be
explain: As per IS classification, first class bricks require a minimum compressive strength of 100 kg/cm2.

q: 25. The minimum compressive strength of 2nd class bricks should be
explain: Second class bricks have a lower minimum compressive strength requirement of about 75 kg/cm2.

q: 26. A 1st class brick immersed in water for 24 hours, should not absorb water (by weight) more than
explain: First class bricks must not absorb more than about 15% of their weight in water after 24-hour immersion.

q: 27. The main ingredient of a good quality brick earth, is
explain: Silica is the principal bulk ingredient of brick earth, giving the brick its basic structure.

q: 28. Clay and silt content in a good brick earth must be at least
explain: Good brick earth needs at least 50% clay and silt content to provide sufficient plasticity for molding.

q: 29. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as
explain: A queen closer is a brick cut so its length equals a full brick but its width is halved.

q: 30. The portion of the brick without a triangular corner equal to half the width and half the length, is called
explain: A king closer has a triangular section removed, leaving half-width and half-length, used to adjust bonding at corners.

q: 31. Refractory bricks resist
explain: Refractory bricks are specially manufactured to withstand very high temperatures without deforming, as used in furnace linings.

q: 32. Sewer pipes are made of
explain: Stoneware is dense, vitrified, and chemically resistant, ideal for carrying sewage.

q: 33. Glazing of clay products, is done
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing gives an impervious, attractive coating that protects clay products from weathering and corrosion.

q: 34. A pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill kneads and tempers clay to a uniform, workable consistency free of air pockets before molding.

q: 35. Generally wooden moulds are made from
explain: Shisham wood is strong, durable, and easy to work, making it a preferred material for brick moulds.

q: 36. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous kiln capable of year-round operation, unlike intermittent clamps or Bull's trench kilns.

q: 37. Plaster of Paris is obtained by calcining
explain: Plaster of Paris is made by heating (calcining) gypsum to partly remove its water of crystallization.

q: 38. For the manufacture of Portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are
explain: Portland cement raw materials are proportioned at roughly 63% lime, 22% silica, and 15% other ingredients.

q: 39. Good quality cement contains higher percentage of
explain: A higher proportion of tricalcium silicate (C3S) gives cement better early strength and overall quality.

q: 40. In the cement the compound quickest to react with water, is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts almost instantly with water, causing flash set if not controlled by gypsum.

q: 41. Rapid hardening cement contains
explain: Rapid hardening cement has a higher C3S content, which speeds up early strength development.

q: 42. Initial setting of cement is caused due to
explain: C3A hydrates very rapidly and is primarily responsible for the initial setting of cement.

q: 43. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and provides the long-term ultimate strength of cement.

q: 44. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding to slow down the fast reaction of C3A, retarding initial setting.

q: 45. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts with water immediately and is the first compound to set.

q: 46. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is
explain: Limestone is the principal raw material, supplying the calcium required for cement manufacture.

q: 47. The percentage of water required for normal consistency for OPC cement, is
explain: For OPC, the standard consistency test typically requires water content between 26% and 33% by weight of cement.

q: 48. Apparatus for Soundness test of cement is
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures cement paste expansion, used to determine soundness.

q: 49. Soundness test of cement determines
explain: The soundness test checks for excess free lime or magnesia, which can cause delayed expansion and cracking.

q: 50. The ability of cement to maintain a constant volume is called
explain: Soundness is defined as cement's ability to retain a constant volume after setting without expansion.

q: 51. Strength of cement concrete primarily depends upon
explain: The water-cement ratio is the dominant factor governing the strength of hardened concrete.

q: 52. White cement should have least percentage of
explain: Iron oxide imparts grey/brown color to ordinary cement, so white cement is made with minimal iron oxide.

q: 53. The insoluble residue in cement is less than
explain: Specifications limit the insoluble residue (impurities) in cement to less than about 1.5%.

q: 54. For a 50 kg cement bag water required, is
explain: For a standard 50 kg cement bag, about 22.5 litres of water is typically used based on standard mix proportions.

q: 55. Minimum required water cement ratio for a workable concrete, is
explain: A minimum water-cement ratio of about 0.40 is generally needed to make concrete workable.

q: 56. A volatile substance added to a paint to make its application easy and smooth, is known as
explain: A solvent (thinner) is a volatile liquid that reduces paint viscosity for smoother application, evaporating afterward.

q: 57. Pigments are available in the form of
explain: Pigments are typically supplied as fine powders, later mixed with a vehicle to form paint.

q: 58. Turpentine oil is used in paints as
explain: Turpentine oil is used as a thinner to reduce paint viscosity for easier application.

q: 59. The most important constituent of varnish, is
explain: Resin is the essential film-forming ingredient of varnish, giving it its glossy, protective finish.

q: 60. A prime coat is given to steel work with
options: a mixture of white lead and lead paint
explain: A prime coat containing white lead/red lead is applied to steel work to prevent rusting before final painting.

q: 61. The base material for distemper, is
explain: Distemper's base material is chalk (whiting), combined with glue and pigments.

q: 62. Distemper is
options: a paint consisting of powdered chalk, pigments, and water
a paint consisting of coloured cement and water
explain: Distemper is a water-based paint made of powdered chalk, pigment, and a glue/water binder.

q: 63. Plastic asphalt is
options: used as a water proofing layer over roof
a mixture of cement and asphalt
explain: Plastic asphalt, being flexible and impermeable, is applied as a waterproofing layer over roofs.

q: 64. Bituminous fells are used for
explain: Bituminous felts are commonly used as damp-proof courses (DPC) to block rising moisture in walls.

q: 65. Quick lime is
explain: Quicklime is chemically calcium oxide (CaO), produced by burning (calcining) limestone.

q: 66. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is
explain: Red lead is used as an anti-corrosive pigment, especially in primers for steel.

q: 67. Oil varnish generally consists of
explain: Oil varnish is typically made by combining oil, resin, and wax to form a protective coating.

q: 68. Bitumen paints offer
explain: Bitumen paints form a tough, waterproof coating mainly valued for its protective (anti-corrosive) qualities.

q: 69. Snowcrete is one of the patent forms of
explain: Snowcem is a well-known brand of waterproof cement paint.

q: 70. The most fire resistant paint are
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant because asbestos itself is a non-combustible mineral fiber.

q: 71. To give a brilliant finish, the type of varnish used, is
explain: Spirit varnish, made by dissolving resin in spirit, dries quickly to give a brilliant glossy finish.

q: 72. The most durable varnish is
explain: Though slower to dry, oil varnish forms the most durable and weather-resistant film.

q: 73. Mastic asphalt is generally used for
explain: Mastic asphalt is dense and impermeable, so it serves as both a damp-proof course and a waterproof layer.

q: 74. Bitumen is generally obtained from
explain: Bitumen is typically a residue obtained from the refining (fractional distillation) of petroleum.

q: 75. Plastic bitumen is generally used for
explain: Being pliable, plastic bitumen is well suited to filling cracks and small gaps in construction.
